chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from some of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

About the man who rises in the last part of the night and raises his voice with the Quran, he said: 'It is appropriate for a man, when he prays at night, to let his family hear him, so that the one who should rise will rise, and the one who should move will move.'

key_terms.آخِرِ اللَّيْلِ: the last part of the night
key_terms.يَقُومَ الْقَائِمُ: the one who should rise will rise

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on raising one's voice during night prayer to wake or remind family members?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the communal aspect of *Qiyam al-Layl* by instructing that one's recitation should be audible to family members, thereby serving as a spiritual catalyst for them to rise and join in worship. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that night prayer is not merely an individual act of devotion but a means of fostering collective piety within the household. The guidance underscores the importance of vocal recitation as a practical tool for inspiring others to engage in spiritual movement and remembrance.
